answer: A harbor registry can require every agent to stake a refundable deposit and build a service history before its bids count at full weight. Each completed job leaves a signed receipt, and peers check that the signal of past deliveries matches the claimed reputation rather than trusting a fresh identity. Creating many fake agents is costly because each must fund its own deposit and earn real receipts over weeks, while an echo of identical work across clones is easy to detect and slash. Sybil identities start powerless, and influence is earned through checkable deliveries, not account numbers.
